indicators.note: the doctor goes into the prison, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic arriving at a jail is searched on the way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' looks like a verb for searching a prisoner, but it is the noun sense of a playful leap; 'entering' puts the doctor inside the British-spelt prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisk is a lively skip or caper, the same as a playful leap about.

clue.text: Finish up having a drink outside for pleasure

indicators.note: the drink goes around the outside of the other piece

parts.note: a glass of something is a drink

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone happily draining a drink at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the finish round, since this is a down entry read from the bottom, and 'outside' wraps the drink around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladness is joy or delight, a state of happiness.

clue.text: Battle remembered in the long run

definitions.meaning: a famous Greek victory over the Persians in 490 BC
a running race of about 26 miles

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek battle gave its name to the long-distance footrace, after the messenger who ran from it to Athens.

parts.note: a better is read as improved, but here it is someone who bets, offered a price by a bookmaker

explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers quote a gambler these figures as the price of a wager.

indicators.note: the busy word sits outside the little word at, wrapping round it

parts.note: busy means active
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bustling about outdoors from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' sounds like a place to be busy, but it tells you the busy word wraps round 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: To start a machine or process is to set it going, switch it on.

definitions.meaning: a secondary condition that makes an illness worse

explanation.definitionFit: The medical sense is a secondary problem worsening an illness; the everyday sense is any snag that makes things harder.

clue.text: Trendy accountant who lived in S America

parts.note: in means fashionable
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A fashionable bookkeeper who once made a home in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inca empire ruled the Andes from Peru before the Spanish conquest; 'who lived' is fair for a people now gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca people ruled an Andean empire in Peru before the Spanish conquest.

parts.note: suggests a sentry, but it is the chain on a pocket watch, named after Queen Victoria's consort

explanation.definitionFit: A watch chain fastened to a waistcoat is named after Queen Victoria's husband, who popularised it.

parts.note: E for east, the Orient
to merge is to blend together

explanation.surface: A newly released Eastern mixture of tea or spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a noun, as in a release, but it is the verb: come out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue forth is to come out into view.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: new tells you the letters of bread are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to mill a fresh loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the rearranging of the loaf's letters; the surface's miller is a red herring for the sense of wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away by rubbing, as grinding does.

indicators.note: the note is placed in the phrase a message, between its two parts

parts.note: taken as written
a cable is a telegram, a sent message
mi (or me) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A warm little line tucked inside a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: MI from the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi) goes into A CABLE, a cable being an old word for a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means good-natured and cordial, on peaceful terms.

parts.note: sounds like a dispute where both parties are justified, but it means having a right hand on each side, equally skilful with either

explanation.definitionFit: Someone equally able with both hands is, jokingly, right-handed on both sides.

definitions.meaning: to write something down, jot it
a single musical sound or a written symbol for one

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both jotting something down for later and a single musical tone.

definitions.meaning: gave off a bad odour, in the British past tense of the verb for sniffing

explanation.definitionFit: The small fish shares its spelling with the British past tense of the verb meaning to give off an odour, as rotten food does.

clue.text: Died on the mat from an overdose of this?

definitions.text: Died on the mat from an overdose of this?

parts.note: d. is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees
a rug is a small floor mat

explanation.surface: A person found dead on the floor after taking too much of something.
explanation.walkthrough: D sits on top of RUG, and the whole clue paints the scene of a fatal overdose, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdose of a narcotic or medicine can kill, leaving the victim on the floor.

definitions.meaning: got to one's feet, past tense
as in 'he ... a round', treated others

explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of getting to one's feet also means treated others to a round in a pub.

clue.text: I'd lifted the front part of a seat

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means the letters are raised, read upwards and so turned round

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
the van is the vanguard, the front part of an army

explanation.surface: Someone raising the front of a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns ID to DI; VAN is short for vanguard. A divan is a backless couch or bed base.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low backless couch or sofa.

clue.text: It's a fault taking the path of less resistance

definitions.text: It's a fault taking the path of less resistance

parts.words: It's a fault taking the path of less resistance
parts.note: an electrical fault where current bypasses its intended route and takes a low-resistance shortcut, playing on the idiom 'path of least resistance'

explanation.definitionFit: This electrical fault happens when current finds an unintended low-resistance route between conductors.

definitions.meaning: moved ahead, made earlier or put forward

explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to lend it, and to advance something is to move it forward.

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl is placed over, above, the weight

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A remark broadcast that a young woman is too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'overweight' as 'over weight': ANN goes above OUNCE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something is to proclaim it publicly.

clue.text: Where to hear opera company putting on unusually grand event

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of grand event are laid out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A troupe staging an exceptionally grand occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' shuffles the letters of 'grand event'. The Royal Opera House stands in this London district, so the name stands for the opera company itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Opera House stands in this London district, so its name is shorthand for that opera venue.

parts.note: someone putting up a barrier to thwart intruders, and also a sportsman with a foil, a light sword

explanation.definitionFit: A swordsman wielding a foil, and jokingly someone building a barrier against intruders.

definitions.meaning: informal word for a lively party

explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent heavily, and informally a big lively celebration.

parts.note: reflection reads as careful thought, but here it is a sound bouncing back off a surface, repeating your words

explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation is your own words returned once sound waves bounce back off a wall or cliff.

clue.text: It's bound to be a shock

definitions.text: It's bound to be a shock

parts.words: It's bound to be a shock
parts.note: shock reads as a fright, but a shock is also a group of sheaves of corn tied and stood up in a field

explanation.definitionFit: A stack of bound sheaves of grain set upright in a field to dry is the farming sense of shock.

clue.text: For this pudding use the back gas-ring

indicators.note: use the back of the word gas, reading it from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written, then turned
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice to cook a dessert on the rear burner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the back' turns GAS into SAG; the ring gives O. 'use' only links. Sago is a starchy pudding staple in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a palm starch cooked with milk into a traditional British milk pudding.

parts.note: a bird whose name, turned round, gives other seabirds, the auks

explanation.definitionFit: This large predatory seabird's name read backwards spells the plural of another seabird.

clue.text: Take off a ring, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for a ring is spoken and matches another spelling

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

explanation.surface: Removing a wedding ring, according to a rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a ring' suggests jewellery, but PEAL is a ring of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove skin or rind is to strip it off.

parts.note: to have a crack at something is to try it
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone appalled at the idea of experimenting with marijuana.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an invitation to sample drugs; instead CRACK (attempt) is followed by POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or mad person, and the word is used as an adjective for wild ideas.

clue.text: Find company in one churchman or another

indicators.note: company is found in the first churchman, placed inside his title

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric heading a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A priest looking for companionship among the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one churchman or another' splits: the first gives the wordplay, 'another' defines a second churchman. 'Find' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Another churchman, as a deacon is an ordained minister ranking below a priest.

clue.text: Take part in a dramatic trial

definitions.text: Take part in a dramatic trial

parts.words: Take part in a dramatic trial
parts.note: trial suggests a sensational court case, but here it is a practice run of a play, where an actor goes over a part

explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise a play before performing it, going over their lines and moves.

clue.text: Take it if you mean to stay dry

definitions.text: Take it if you mean to stay dry

parts.words: Take it if you mean to stay dry
parts.note: staying dry sounds like avoiding rain, but it means giving up alcohol by taking a formal vow of abstinence

explanation.definitionFit: To take this solemn promise is to vow to abstain from alcohol.
